title: Memory Is Now In Harvey
format_note: Music-only feature announcement: a preference question, a real-UI memory demo, personas each carrying their own remembered preferences, then a four-line brand sign-off.
one_thing: Harvey now remembers each lawyer's working preferences and applies them across every place they work.

transcript.voice_style: No speech. Caption track absent; local whisper returned only '.' segments. All meaning is carried by on-screen text.
transcript.script_shape: Question card, answer chips, product name, UI proof, 'Applied everywhere you work', four persona orbits, then 'Your Preferences. Your Work. Your Harvey. Harvey'.

structure.frame0: Empty paper-texture ground with the question card 'When you send me a contract, how do you want the review back?' on screen from the first sampled frame (f0001.jpg), centred and 43% of frame width.
structure.first_3s: The card drifts up about 14 px, then at 2.9-4 s it grows a menu of four review formats and 'Type something else...' (f0003.jpg). The subject is present throughout.

beats.what: Question card asks how the lawyer wants contract review back; four options unfold.
Cursor picks 'Short summary the business can read'; the menu slides left and a chip splits off.
Menu leaves, dashed rings appear, a planet labelled Maya, Commercial Counsel arrives with three preference chips.
Hard cut to 'Introducing' then 'Harvey Memory' on a bare paper ground.
Real Harvey chat: user states a colour-coding preference, 'Memories saved' card types out, then a second thread opens a memo.
Memory tab lists three memories; the memo scrolls with chips beside it and the matching headings highlighted.
'Applied everywhere you work' with the chips' icons swapping to Outlook and Word.
Persona orbits for Omar, Eleanor, Rob and Priya, each with their own preference chips.
Four centred lines swap one word at a time: Your Preferences. Your Work. Your Harvey. Harvey.

hero_moment.what: Memo with 'Executive Summary' highlighted while the chip 'My GC prefers numbered lists' sits beside it, connecting a stored preference to its visible effect (f0019.jpg).

ending.cta_text: Your Preferences. Your Work. Your Harvey. Harvey
ending.what: Plain serif wordmark centred on the paper ground; no button, no URL. Hold under 2.6 s is inferred from a 6 s static run ending at 66 s, so approximate.

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: Almost nothing is cut. The 39.5 s shot from 21 s to 60.54 s holds 58% of runtime. Interest comes from internal motion: menu unfold, card slides, chip fly-ins, scroll, persona swaps every 1-2 s.

look.ground: Off-white paper with soft grey painted blocks that shift position from scene to scene; light share 1.0, luma 238.7 in look.json.
look.accent_use: Teal appears only on the memory icon and the memo highlights, so colour means 'memory'. Planets are the only dark mass.
look.type: Large serif display for titles ('Harvey Memory' pairs light serif with bold sans-like 'Memory'); small grotesque for UI chips and labels; role lines in grey.
look.depth: Soft drop shadows lift cards off the paper; planets are shaded spheres; dashed concentric rings give an orbit. UI is a flat window with a shadow.

product_ui.camera_on_ui: At 21-33 s the window is shown whole, then punched in so the chat fills the frame (f0013.jpg), then pulled out. At 36-44 s the view pans to the Memory panel and memo.
product_ui.notes: Chip and card text is about 20 px on 720 p and reads. Memo body and sidebar text is about 9 px and does not; the message survives because enlarged chips and highlights repeat it beside the document.

motion.text_entry: Titles fade in and settle in place; 'Introducing' appears first and 'Harvey Memory' arrives about 0.33 s later (strips/window-09-17.417s.jpg). Closing lines swap words in place.
motion.ui_motion: Menu unfolds, then slides off left while the chosen chip detaches and stays; chips pop in around the planet; 'Memories saved' text types out; memory list rows append.
motion.camera: Slow zoom-out as rings arrive; zoom-in on the chat; pan across the memo. Planet counts drift slightly with rotation of the surface.
motion.eases: Soft ease-out on card slides, about 0.4 s; chips drift continuously; no overshoot visible in the strips I opened.

transitions.cause: Title card to product window; scene change under the title.
Menu slides off after the cursor picks an option, leaving the chosen chip.
Reply appears, memory card types out, panel tab fills.
Rings and planet arrive as the camera pulls back.
Persona planet, name and chips swap in place on the same orbit template.

good.observation: The film opens on the question the product answers, shown as a real-looking interface card on a calm ground. The viewer is asked something before being told anything.
Interaction explains the feature: the cursor picks an option and the chosen chip survives while the menu leaves. Choice becomes memory without a word of narration.
A single reusable orbit template (planet, name, role, three chips) carries four personas, so the idea of 'everyone's own preferences' is shown by repetition and swap.
Real product UI shows the preference landing in an output: chip beside the memo, matching headings highlighted in teal.
Restraint: one ground, one accent colour, no cross-dissolves; only 4 hard cuts in 67.8 s and a 39.5 s continuous shot.
The sign-off swaps one word per line, ending on the brand name alone, which compresses the message into a rhythm the viewer can finish.

weak.observation: Memo body, sidebar and memory-panel text is about 9 px on a 720 p frame and unreadable at phone width; the proof relies on the chips beside it.
No call to action, URL or availability line at the end; the film ends on the wordmark only.
Persona chips are held 1.4-2 s and several are truncated with an ellipsis ('Refer US state privacy to Ba...'), so the specifics are not readable in time.

rule_candidates.rule: A calm explainer can open with the subject already on screen as a single centred card at 40-45% of frame width and hold it 4 s before expanding it.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0001.jpg card 553 of 1280 px wide; menu opens at 2.9 s

rule_candidates.rule: A feature film can run with a median shot of 7 s and one 39 s shot if something on screen changes every 1-2 s; judge pace by on-screen change rather than cut count.
rule_candidates.evidence: metrics.json median_shot_s 7.24, longest_shot 39.54 s; strips 12 and 28

rule_candidates.rule: Show a product capability through a cause on screen: cursor picks an option, the menu slides off, the chosen chip stays and becomes the next scene's subject.
When real UI text is under 10 px, repeat its fact as a chip at 20 px or more beside it and highlight the matching spot in the UI.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0019.jpg chip text ~21 px, memo text ~9 px

rule_candidates.rule: Build one repeatable template (hero object, name, role, three chips) and swap its content every 1.4-2 s to show variety without new layouts.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0028-f0030.jpg, strip 28: Rob to Priya at 59.29 s

rule_candidates.rule: A quiet launch film needs no cut burst: 0 bursts, 4 cuts in 67.8 s worked when motion lived inside shots.
Close with 3-4 two-word lines that change one word each time, the last being the brand name alone, each at 5.8-8% of frame height.
